what_it_is: Star reviews and written feedback on your own listings, app store page or Google profile
who_it_over_represents: The delighted and the furious. Review distributions are J-shaped: ratings pile at 5 and 1, so the middle of your customer base is close to absent
what_it_cannot_see: Everyone who bought and said nothing, which is the large majority, and everyone who considered and did not buy
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: 30 reviews before a complaint is a theme; below that the J-shape makes any sample look polarised
rights_note: The review text is the author's copyright. The platform's terms of service license the platform, not you. Quoting a named customer in an ad needs their consent regardless of copyright
strongest_claim_it_supports: What a buyer chose to say in public once the purchase was already behind them
what_it_does_not_establish: Why they bought. A review is written by somebody who has already decided, so it explains satisfaction and not choice

what_it_is: Pre-purchase questions left on a product listing, and the answers other buyers gave
who_it_over_represents: The cautious buyer who reads the whole page and is willing to wait for an answer
what_it_cannot_see: The buyer who had the same doubt and left instead of typing it
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: 15 questions on one listing, or the same question on 3 listings
rights_note: Same as a review: the asker wrote it. Use it to fix the page, not as a testimonial
strongest_claim_it_supports: The specific objections your listing copy failed to answer, in the buyer's own words
what_it_does_not_establish: How many silent buyers shared the doubt. Asking a public question is a rare and motivated act

what_it_is: The reason code and free-text attached to returns, refunds and cancellations
who_it_over_represents: Reasons that fit the dropdown, and buyers for whom returning was cheap and easy
what_it_cannot_see: The customer who kept the thing, disliked it and simply never bought again
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: 20 returns, and read the free-text before trusting any code
rights_note: Transaction data tied to an identifiable person. Report it aggregated and never quote a named return
strongest_claim_it_supports: The size of the gap between what the page promised and what arrived
what_it_does_not_establish: Which side moved. A mismatch code says the expectation and the product disagreed, not whose fault that was

what_it_is: Inbound support conversations, their categories and their resolution notes
who_it_over_represents: People who believe complaining works, and problems severe enough to be worth the effort of reporting
what_it_cannot_see: Silent abandonment. The ratio of silent to vocal is unknown from inside the queue and is usually the larger number
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: 25 tickets in a category before it is a product problem rather than a run of bad luck
rights_note: A support conversation is private and usually holds order and contact details. Code it, do not paste it
strongest_claim_it_supports: Which failures are costing you labour, ranked by what they cost
what_it_does_not_establish: How often the failure happens in the customer base. A ticket count measures reporting, not incidence

what_it_is: Zalo, Messenger, WhatsApp and livestream comment threads where the pre-purchase conversation actually happens
who_it_over_represents: Buyers who need reassurance from a human before paying, which in Vietnamese social commerce is most of them
what_it_cannot_see: The scroll-past. Nobody messages to say they were not interested
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: 30 conversations, sampled across days and across whoever was replying
rights_note: A private message. Even with the customer's blessing, screenshots leak the account name and the thread above
strongest_claim_it_supports: The exact words a buyer uses for the problem before anybody has taught them yours, which is the best raw material for copy that exists
what_it_does_not_establish: Prevalence of anything. People who did not open a chat are structurally invisible here

what_it_is: CRM notes and call summaries written by whoever was selling
who_it_over_represents: What the rep found memorable, and whatever confirms the rep's existing theory of the deal
what_it_cannot_see: What the buyer did not get to say because the rep was talking, and the deals nobody logged
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: 20 calls spread across at least 3 different reps, or you are studying one rep
rights_note: Internal record about a named prospect. It is also hearsay: attributing a quote to a customer from a rep's note misrepresents both
strongest_claim_it_supports: The objections that surface under commercial pressure, which are not the ones a survey collects
what_it_does_not_establish: The buyer's language. A note is a paraphrase, and a paraphrase has already been coded by somebody with a quota

what_it_is: Structured conversations with buyers who chose you and buyers who chose somebody else, run after the decision
who_it_over_represents: Losses willing to take the call, which skews toward the ones who liked you enough to be polite
what_it_cannot_see: The buyer who never entered your process, and the one who bought nothing at all
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: 12 interviews for the code set, 20 before quoting a share; wins and losses counted separately
rights_note: Get recording consent explicitly and separately from quoting consent. A B2B buyer's employer may also have a say
strongest_claim_it_supports: The criterion that actually decided a specific deal, and whether your positioning was even in the room
what_it_does_not_establish: The real reason, as distinct from the reportable one. Post-hoc rationalisation and cause are indistinguishable in an interview

what_it_is: The question asked at cancellation, plus whatever the customer typed into it
who_it_over_represents: The last irritation, and customers annoyed enough to answer on the way out
what_it_cannot_see: The decision, which was usually made weeks before the cancel button
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: 25 responses per plan or segment, because churn reasons differ by what they were paying
rights_note: Attached to an account. Aggregate before it leaves the tool
strongest_claim_it_supports: The stated trigger, and the share of leavers who name a reason you can act on
what_it_does_not_establish: Cause. An exit reason is the last straw and tells you nothing about the load that was already there

what_it_is: A timeline interview reconstructing the events between first thought and purchase, for somebody who recently switched
who_it_over_represents: Recent switchers who can be found and are willing to spend an hour, and stories tidy enough to retell
what_it_cannot_see: The people who considered switching and stayed put, who are the counterfactual the whole exercise needs
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: 12 interviews before the code set stops growing, 16 to 24 before the interpretation is stable
rights_note: Consent to record, consent to quote, and a stated retention period. Incentives are fine and must be disclosed in the writeup
strongest_claim_it_supports: The sequence of events and the specific moment that made the status quo unacceptable
what_it_does_not_establish: That the same sequence will work again, or that the customer's ordering of events is the real ordering

what_it_is: Watching somebody buy, unbox, cook, install or use the thing, with as little instruction as you can manage
who_it_over_represents: People who agree to be watched, and behaviour performed for an audience
what_it_cannot_see: What they do when nobody is in the room, which is the behaviour you are actually selling into
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: 5 sessions to find most single-cause usability failures; prevalence needs a different method entirely
rights_note: Filming a person in their home or shop needs written consent, and anybody else in frame has not consented
strongest_claim_it_supports: Where the workaround is, and which step the product's own instructions get wrong
what_it_does_not_establish: How many customers hit the problem. Five sessions is a discovery sample and carries no share

what_it_is: Keyword volume from a search tool, plus the queries typed into your own site search
who_it_over_represents: Demand that already has a word for itself and knows to type it
what_it_cannot_see: The need with no vocabulary yet, which is where a new category lives, and everything happening inside apps and closed platforms
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: One full month of site search, or a keyword set with volume the tool will state a range for
rights_note: A single site-search query can identify a person, especially a long one. Report counts, never the query log
strongest_claim_it_supports: The relative size of stated demand, and the words the market uses instead of yours
what_it_does_not_establish: Intent behind the words. A price query is a shopper, a complainer or a competitor, and the string is identical

what_it_is: Funnel, cohort and event data from the site, app or checkout
who_it_over_represents: Consented, unblocked, single-device traffic
what_it_cannot_see: Reasons, and any journey that crosses a device or ends in a phone call to your shop
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: Whatever makes the interval on the step you care about narrower than the decision you are making
rights_note: Consent state governs what you may collect at all, and the answer differs by market
strongest_claim_it_supports: What happened, in what order, at what rate, and where it stopped
what_it_does_not_establish: Why, ever. Analytics locates the wound and cannot name the weapon

what_it_is: Replays of individual sessions, with cursor movement, scroll depth and rage clicks
who_it_over_represents: Sessions long enough to look interesting, which is why they get watched
what_it_cannot_see: What the person was trying to do, and everything on the screen the recorder masks
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: 15 recordings filtered to one flow, watched with a coding sheet rather than for entertainment
rights_note: Recordings capture whatever the customer typed, including data you never intended to hold. Masking is a configuration, not a default
strongest_claim_it_supports: Where hesitation happens, and the exact element people abandon on
what_it_does_not_establish: Intent or satisfaction. A long pause is reading, thinking, confusion or a phone call

what_it_is: Facebook groups, Reddit, Zalo groups, sector forums and review-site discussion
who_it_over_represents: The confident poster, and whatever opinion the group has already decided is correct
what_it_cannot_see: Lurkers, who are the overwhelming majority of any community, and anyone the group's norms exclude
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: 20 threads across at least 3 unconnected communities, or you have measured one group's house opinion
rights_note: Public does not mean licensed. A group post is the author's, many groups forbid taking content out, and screenshots carry the poster's name and photo
strongest_claim_it_supports: The vocabulary, the shared assumptions and the accepted workarounds of a specific segment
what_it_does_not_establish: Representativeness of anything. A community selects for people who care enough to join one

what_it_is: Comments, replies and DMs on your own posts and ads
who_it_over_represents: The audience you already converted, plus whoever the algorithm decided to show it to
what_it_cannot_see: The market. This is a census of your existing following and nothing else
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: 30 comments across at least 5 posts, and separate paid comments from organic ones
rights_note: A comment is the commenter's, and re-posting one with the handle visible is publishing a named person's words
strongest_claim_it_supports: What your existing audience rewards with engagement
what_it_does_not_establish: Anything about people who are not already following you. This is the most quoted and least transferable source in the list

what_it_is: Reading the reviews, complaints and questions on products that are not yours
who_it_over_represents: The same two extremes your own reviews over-represent, now for somebody else's product
what_it_cannot_see: What the competitor quietly does well, because satisfied expectation goes unmentioned
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: 40 reviews across at least 2 competitors, so a theme is about the category and not about one bad batch
rights_note: Never reproduce a competitor's review as if it were feedback on you, and check comparative-advertising rules before quoting a rival by name
strongest_claim_it_supports: An unmet need in the category, described by somebody who paid money for the alternative
what_it_does_not_establish: That you can serve the need, that it is worth paying more for, or that the complaint is not the price of something the reviewer also wanted

what_it_is: The score, and more usefully the free-text box under it
who_it_over_represents: The moment immediately after whatever interaction triggered the survey
what_it_cannot_see: Cause, and any customer who dismissed the prompt
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: 25 verbatims for a theme; a score movement needs an interval, not a target
rights_note: Tied to an account. Anonymise before it appears in a deck
strongest_claim_it_supports: A trend in stated sentiment for one touchpoint, when the question and timing are held constant
what_it_does_not_establish: What the score means. The 0-to-10 cut into promoters and detractors is a convention that throws away most of the variance, and comparing your number to an industry benchmark compares two different questionnaires

what_it_is: A structured questionnaire sent to a known list, with a computable response rate
who_it_over_represents: Responders. Non-response bias is the whole methodological problem and it does not shrink as the sample grows
what_it_cannot_see: Non-responders, who differ from responders in ways correlated with what you asked
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: Set by the interval you need, not by a rule of thumb; run scripts/check_evidence_saturation.py --interval before fielding
rights_note: State the purpose and retention at the top of the form. An incentive must be disclosed when the result is published
strongest_claim_it_supports: Prevalence within the population that answered, with an interval attached
what_it_does_not_establish: Prevalence in the customer base, unless the response rate is high or non-response has been modelled. A leading question manufactures its own answer and the arithmetic will still look clean

what_it_is: Asking what somebody would pay, including the four-question Van Westendorp form
who_it_over_represents: Agreeableness, and respondents who want to be helpful about a product they are not buying today
what_it_cannot_see: Behaviour at the till, where the money is real and an alternative is on the next shelf
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: 100 responses per segment, and it is still a hypothesis
rights_note: Do not publish a stated willingness-to-pay figure as a price benchmark; it will be quoted back at you
strongest_claim_it_supports: A range worth testing with a real offer, and the shape of resistance across a segment
what_it_does_not_establish: A price. Stated willingness to pay runs systematically above revealed willingness to pay, so treat the number as a ceiling and the test as the evidence

what_it_is: Third-party or syndicated survey data about a category, bought or read from a published report
who_it_over_represents: Professional respondents, and whichever population the panel could recruit cheaply
what_it_cannot_see: Your buyer specifically, and any question the vendor did not ask
minimum_before_a_theme_counts: Whatever the vendor sampled; demand the n, the field dates and the question wording or do not quote it
rights_note: Redistribution is governed by the report's licence, and a chart redrawn from a paywalled report is still that report's content. Route through market-data-collection.md
strongest_claim_it_supports: Category-level context that sizes an argument you are making for other reasons
what_it_does_not_establish: Anything about your own customers, and nothing at all once the field date is more than a year old in a moving category
